How To use a Safety Razor

With the cost of razor cartridges seeming more and more ridiculous, I've opted to switch to a safety razor for my face. The razor blades are much cheaper, give you much more accuracy for styling purposes, and are -- in all honesty -- very easy to use.

There are really only 3 things that you need to remember when shaving with a safety razor:

  • 30-ish degree blade angle against your skin
  • small strokes
  • Let the weight of the razor do the work

I have yet to cut myself; but maybe I've just jinxed myself by saying so, LoL.

Some might need to use the pre-shave oil, but I just shave before I shower as the oil on my face seems to do the trick. I do recommend you get a non-alcohol based aftershave though, as it goes a long way in helping your face after the shave/shower.

I still use my trusty Gillette Mach 3 to shave my head. It's nearly impossible to use the safety razor in such an awkward position without causing serious razor burn to the back of your head (yes, I did...I looked like a tiger).

They look scary, but they're honestly very safe and easy to use. You'll be laughing at yourself for being so nervous, after the very first time you shave.

Pro - Tip
Change your blade every 3 shaves.
Better to change out before the blade gets dull.
If the blade is pulling the hair and not cutting, the blade is way too dull.
I change the blade every shave. They are 2.5 cents each; after paying 100 times that for each mach 3 razor (which I had to change every other shave) it is a luxury I can afford.
